# The proposal

## Overview

babelrd will be a separate package, as I proposed in [sprint #10](https://github.com/r-devel/r-project-sprint-2026/issues/10), so rdlocal stays free of API keys and network calls. The groundwork in rdlocal (#35, #36) exists; babelrd's own code starts at M1.

```r
rdlocal::i18n_module_create("path/to/MASS", language = "es",
                            module_name = "MASS.es")
babelrd::estimate("MASS.es")                     # cost vs free tiers
babelrd::draft("MASS.es", provider = "deepl")    # key from DEEPL_API_KEY
babelrd::check("MASS.es")                        # per-page report
babelrd::to_po("MASS.es", "MASS-es.po")          # for Weblate or Poedit
babelrd::from_po("MASS.es", "MASS-es.po")        # reviewed strings back in
```

## Detail

### Minimum Viable Product

`draft()` and `check()` with DeepL. Every drafted page passes the checks and every drafted string is `fuzzy`; human translations are never overwritten. rdlocal does show fuzzy strings to readers, with a note that says "may be out of date", so teams publish after review, and I'll propose a machine-draft wording upstream.

### Architecture

1. Protect: `\code{}`, `\link` targets, `\eqn`, `{ISEXPR_n}` and user macros become do-not-translate tags; link text stays translatable.
2. Translate one help page per batch, so terms stay consistent within a page. DeepL comes first because babeldown already uses it and the MASS pilot fits its free tier; r-dev-day #66 prefers Microsoft for bulk (2 million free characters a month against DeepL's 500,000), and it follows in M3 with the [r-devel/glossary](https://github.com/r-devel/glossary) terms.
3. Check: placeholders exactly once, Rd re-parses, the page renders (`tools::Rd2txt()`), glossary terms used. Failing strings stay empty and go in the report.
4. Mark: `fuzzy: yes` plus `machine: <provider> <date>`.
5. PO bridge, in babelrd: `fuzzy` becomes gettext `#, fuzzy`, and `from_po()` skips entries whose `msgid` no longer matches `original`, so stale files can't overwrite newer text.

### Assumptions

- rdlocal's module YAML stays stable or changes additively; I wrote its generator and updater.
- Drafts are good enough that reviewing beats translating. This is the real risk: on R's Weblate, machine drafts let a translator progress "a little faster" but "sometimes got the meaning completely wrong" ([r-dev-day #66](https://github.com/r-devel/r-dev-day/issues/66)). Nothing is marked reviewed automatically, and M4 measures the edit rate.

### External dependencies

Imports yaml and httr2; ellmer is optional. rdlocal is only Suggested (to generate modules), since loading it patches `utils:::.getHelpFile`, so babelrd never touches R's help system and could go to CRAN once rdlocal is in a repository. potools has no exported PO reader, so babelrd carries a small one.

### Failure modes

| Risk | Recovery |
|---|---|
| A provider changes API or terms | Each backend is one small function |
| R's Weblate doesn't take help pages yet | PO files work in Poedit or any gettext editor |
